exact_edits.old:
In particular **products** $F\times_SG$ over the terminal algebraic
space $S$ are algebraic spaces over $S$. The **diagonal**
$\Delta\colon F\to F\times_SF$ is a morphism between algebraic spaces,
representable by schemes by condition 2 of the definition of an algebraic
space, and more generally a morphism of algebraic spaces has property
$\mathcal P$ when it is representable and every base change to a scheme has
$\mathcal P$ ([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]]): in particular it
is **separated** when its diagonal is a closed immersion
([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]), **etale** when it is representable etale,
and an **open immersion** when it is representable by open immersions
([[def-open-immersion-schemes]]).
exact_edits.new:
In particular **products** $F\times_SG$ over the terminal algebraic
space $S$ are algebraic spaces over $S$. The **diagonal**
$\Delta_F\colon F\to F\times_SF$ is a morphism of algebraic spaces
representable by schemes, by condition 2 of
[[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]].

Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of scheme morphisms stable under base change.
For a morphism $f\colon F\to G$ **representable by schemes**, the
**representable property $\mathcal P$** means that every base change
$F\times_GT\to T$ to a scheme has $\mathcal P$
([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]]). In particular, an **open
immersion** is a morphism representable by open immersions
([[def-open-immersion-schemes]]). A morphism $f$ is **separated** when its
relative diagonal $\Delta_f\colon F\to F\times_GF$ is a closed immersion
([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]); this diagonal is representable by
schemes, being a base change of $\Delta_F$.

If $\mathcal P$ is local in the etale topology on both source and target,
it extends to arbitrary morphisms of algebraic spaces by scheme charts:
$f\colon F\to G$ **has property $\mathcal P$** when for every commutative
square with top arrow $h\colon U\to V$, bottom arrow $f$, and representable
etale vertical arrows $U\to F$ and $V\to G$ from schemes, $h$ has
$\mathcal P$. Thus $f$ is **etale** when these scheme morphisms $h$ are
etale ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]). For properties additionally stable
under base change and fppf-local on the target, this chart definition agrees
with the preceding fibrewise definition whenever $f$ is representable by
schemes. In particular **representable etale** requires both scheme
representability and etaleness; a general etale morphism of algebraic spaces
need not be representable by schemes.

source_reading_evidence.evidence: Morphisms of algebraic spaces over S are transformations of functors.
Products of algebraic spaces are algebraic spaces; sheaf, diagonal, and scheme-cover checks are componentwise.
For F,G algebraic spaces and H a sheaf with representable diagonal, F×_H G is algebraic. The diagonal is a pullback of the product diagonals and U×_H V is a scheme cover.
The presheaf fibre product is the algebraic-space categorical fibre product; invokes 65.7.2.
This tag is compatible presentation lifting, not Lemma 65.7.2. The existing locator 02X0-02X2 must be corrected to 02X0,04T9,02X2.

source_reading_evidence.scope_read: Complete Example 65.14.2, including all seven properties and final descent consequence
source_reading_evidence.evidence: For a quadratic Galois k′/k, S=Spec k[x], U=Spec k′[x], R=Δ(U)∐Δ′(U minus 0_U), the quotient X=U/R is algebraic and etale over S but not a scheme. X→S cannot be representable by schemes, since base change by id_S would be X.
General etale f:X→Y means each etale scheme map U→X has etale composite U→Y; the composites from schemes are scheme-representable because Y has representable diagonal.

If P is also arbitrary-base-change-stable and fppf-local on base, the definition agrees with fibrewise P for represented f. This supplies the proposed general property clause with precisely its hypotheses.

proof_audit.existing_fibre_product_argument: Sound: limits of sheaves are objectwise; equality loci of paired sections are fibre products of scheme equality loci of F/G; representability of Δ_H makes W=U_F×_H U_G a scheme; base change to T→F×_H G is (T×_F U_F)×_T(T×_G U_G), an etale surjective scheme over T. This proves the full original scope without choosing lifts to a cover of H. No change to this argument is proposed.
proof_audit.relative_diagonal: For f:F→G, Δ_f is the pullback of Δ_F along F×_G F→F×_S F and is therefore representable by schemes; defining separatedness by closed immersion does not demand representability of f.
proof_audit.chart_properties: The source-and-target-locality hypothesis is essential to the general chart clause. Mere base-change stability supports only the represented fibrewise clause. The additional fppf-locality-on-target condition is stated where equivalence of the two extensions is claimed.
proof_audit.source_consistency: The etale chart criterion is precisely §66.16 and §67.22; represents no restriction of etale maps to scheme-representable maps. Every scheme-domain map to an algebraic space is scheme-representable via pullback of its target diagonal.
